summary: ITER-131 backend-only regression for the bcrypt → asyncio.to_thread scheduling fix. Wrote /app/backend/tests/test_iter131_bcrypt_async.py covering login (admin+manager, correct+wrong pw), MFA verify (correct+wrong OTP with DB override), password change round-trip, admin-create-user + new-user login, backend health/startup, and a concurrency proof (login in flight while 15 concurrent /api/health pings). 9/10 tests passed, 1 skipped (manager MFA is now genuinely optional per the Sep 2026 Supabase-migration change and was disabled on this seed, so the wrong-OTP test cannot be exercised without first enabling MFA — skip is correct behaviour, not a failure). Concurrency claim verified end-to-end: with a 2.7s admin login in flight (multiple bcrypt hashes + Supabase HTTP), 15 concurrent /api/health pings returned with median=8.8ms, p95=12.9ms — event loop is clearly NOT blocked. All bcrypt call sites in auth.py/admin.py/super_admin.py/org.py/utils/seed.py verified to correctly `await hash_password` / `await verify_password`. Backend logs show clean startup, no exceptions from seed_super_admin.

minor.issue: When a user has migrated to Supabase (supabase_password_set=TRUE), a wrong current_password surfaces as 401 (from supabase verify_login) rather than the code's own 400 'Current password is incorrect'. Pre-existing behaviour, unrelated to this fix — both status codes correctly reject the request, but the error contract differs across bcrypt vs Supabase users. Test was updated to accept 400 or 401.

Helper script broken — passes isoformat string as $2 to a timestamptz column, raises asyncpg.DataError. Not our fix's fault but worth flagging for maintenance; worked around inline in test setup. Pre-existing helper drift.

action_items: None required for the bcrypt-async fix — it is functionally correct and the concurrency claim is verified.

(Optional cleanup, unrelated to this fix) Fix tests/reset_test_pw.py: pass datetime object (not .isoformat() string) to the timestamptz parameter, or drop the password_changed_at column from the UPDATE.

(Optional cleanup, unrelated to this fix) Consider normalising the /api/auth/change-password wrong-current-password response so bcrypt and Supabase paths both return 400 (not one 400 / one 401) for a consistent client contract.
critical_code_review_comments: hash_password/verify_password in routers/auth.py cleanly use asyncio.to_thread — correct primitive; won't wedge event loop.
All 8 bcrypt call sites in auth.py (2 wrapper defs + 3 raw hashpw/checkpw sites in _generate_and_send_mfa/verify_mfa/toggle_mfa + callers) confirmed awaited.
admin.py, super_admin.py, org.py, utils/seed.py all use `await hash_password(...)` — verified via grep, no un-awaited coroutines remaining.
seed.py:3838 correctly awaits inside the seed function; startup logs are clean.
test_credentials: admin@supervision.com/Admin123! (bcrypt path), manager@supervision.com/Manager123! (bcrypt path, restored). Reset manager's password + flipped supabase_password_set back to FALSE after the change-password round trip to preserve the bcrypt-path baseline for future runs.
seed_data_creation: None retained. Test creates a `TEST_iter131_*@example.com` attendee user via admin API and deletes it in the same test's finally block. login_attempts table is DELETEd at the start of each rate-limit-sensitive test.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Concurrency proof: with a real admin login in flight (~2.7s wall-clock including bcrypt+Supabase), 15 concurrent /api/health pings return in <35ms each — event loop is not blocked. If a future regression re-introduces sync bcrypt, this test will catch it (median will jump to ~200ms+). MFA wrong-OTP test is currently skipped because manager MFA is optional per Sep-2026 policy change; if MFA is re-enabled for manager, un-skip that assertion. reset_test_pw.py is currently broken (pre-existing), so I did the manager pw reset inline via asyncpg — see the ad-hoc script in this iteration's shell history if you need to re-do it.
rca of the issue: N/A — this iteration is a testing/verification pass over an already-applied scheduling fix (bcrypt work moved from event loop thread into asyncio.to_thread worker threads). No new bug found.
